title: What Is the Back-End Process? A Beginner's Guide to the Assembly and Packaging Steps That Make Semiconductor Chips Usable
excerpt: The back-end process cuts out the semiconductor circuits made in the front-end process, connects them, encapsulates them, and tests them to make products. For beginners, we explain dicing, bonding, molding, and final testing, plus words to look for in job postings, how jobs for people new to semiconductors differ from technical jobs, and the path to advanced packaging.
